sections.heading: What is trending: “centre de données”
paragraphs: “centre de données” appeared on Google Trends' Trending Now list for BE (snapshot taken 2026-11-27T18:58:49+00:00 UTC). Google reports at least 2,000 searches for this term — that figure is a lower bound published in the official Trends feed, not an exact count.

sections.heading: What's behind the spike — the coverage
paragraphs: The Trends feed associates this search spike with 3 news stories from L'Echo, La Libre.be, Le Soir. The headlines, exactly as published:
list: “La Wallonie impose l'arrêt du chantier du data center de Google à Aiseau-Presles, faute de permis” — L'Echo
“Des agents de la Région wallonne procéderont à des vérifications sur le chantier Google à Farciennes” — Le Soir
“Le data center de Google en cours de construction à Aiseau-Presles, souligne Farciennes” — La Libre.be

sections.heading: Timeline
paragraphs: The trend entry was published to the Google Trends feed at Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:40:00 -0800. Our snapshot was taken at 2026-11-27T18:58:49+00:00 UTC and this briefing was assembled at 2026-11-27T18:59:12+00:00 UTC.

sections.heading: How to read these numbers
paragraphs: Google Trends reports approximate search volume as a lower bound (for example “20K+”). Actual volume can be significantly higher. Trending status reflects acceleration in searches, not the absolute size of a topic. For the full story behind the spike, read the cited coverage below — this briefing intentionally adds no speculation beyond the sourced facts.

faq.a: Google's Trending Now feed links the spike to coverage from L'Echo, La Libre.be, Le Soir. The associated headlines are: “La Wallonie impose l'arrêt du chantier du data center de Google à Aiseau-Presles, faute de permis” (L'Echo); “Des agents de la Région wallonne procéderont à des vérifications sur le chantier Google à Farciennes” (Le Soir); “Le data center de Google en cours de construction à Aiseau-Presles, souligne Farciennes” (La Libre.be).

faq.q: How many people searched for “centre de données”?
faq.a: Google reports at least 2,000 searches in BE as of the feed snapshot. This is a published lower bound, not an exact count.
This snapshot covers BE. The same term may trend differently in other regions.
